title: Plant comparison table
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Skeletons, muscles, nutrition and plants (Tribal Tales)
source: Seeded from science/y3 lesson 20 (Plant comparison table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 20: Comparing plants around the home. To understand that different plants have parts that look different but do the same jobs

questions.q: Look at the photo of a spider plant. Describe its leaves.
questions.model: Shape: long and thin like a ribbon. Colour: green with white stripes. So: long, thin, striped leaves.

questions.q: Does every plant have flowers all year?
questions.a: No, many flower only at certain times

questions.q: Which part of a cactus stores water?
Choose two plants at home (houseplant, herb pot, garden plant or vegetables). Fill in the comparison table on the sheet.
questions.a: Pupils' own; for example basil: oval soft leaves, thin stem; aloe: thick spiky leaves
questions.model: Teacher fills in Plant A on camera with a mint plant: 'Leaves: oval and crinkly; stem: thin and square; no flowers today.'

questions.q: Write one way your two plants are the same and one way they are different.
questions.a: For example: both have green leaves; one has flowers and one does not.

questions.q: Why might a plant on a windowsill lean towards the window?
questions.a: It grows towards the light to make more food.
Find what is the same and different
options: Find what is the same and different

questions.q: Big question: why do a cactus and a lettuce look so different?
questions.a: They are suited to different places; the cactus stores water and saves it.
